analysis.headline: Lloyd's Original Return Ends Before a Separate Reacquisition
analysis.analysis: Stilly drafted Brooks in round nine; Thommy drafted Lloyd in round eleven. Stilly started Lloyd and Hall in Week 1 while Jacobs and Henderson were on the bench. Thommy started Achane and Stevenson with Brooks on the bench. Original trade ownership began August 31 and ended October 3 when Lloyd was dropped for Emanuel Wilson. Lloyd returned October 7 via add dropping Keon Coleman, then was dropped October 21 in a waiver acquisition of C.J. Stroud. Week 1 and 2 starter points were 3.70 and 7.60; Week 6 starter point was 1.00 after reacquisition. Original trade direct starter return is 11.30 across two starts (5.65 per start) in these verified snapshots, not 12.30 across three. Week 3 and 5 bench scores were 2.80 and 16.20; Week 4 roster did not include Lloyd. Brooks appeared on Thommy's Week 11 bench. Full Brooks ownership history and exact pretrade roster remain to be reconstructed.
analysis.verdict: Stilly's original return was modest and ended with his first release. The separate free-agent acquisition must not be credited to the trade. Thommy's Week 11 retention leaves potential value unresolved.

analysis.headline: Stew and Scott Exchange Receivers With Different Draft Investments
analysis.analysis: Stew drafted Egbuka in round six and Scott drafted McConkey in round eight. Both were WR-for-WR exchanges, not positional rebalancing. Stew's draft already included Wilson, Flowers, Pittman and Meyers; Scott's top three picks were RBs Robinson, Jeanty and Montgomery, with Moore and Burden among his WR options. Both acquired receivers started Week 1: McConkey 16.70, Egbuka 8.80. McConkey was later traded to Kuhl September 30. Archive totals favor Scott in volume (59.90 across seven starts versus 30.30 across three); Stew leads raw efficiency (10.10 versus 8.56).
analysis.verdict: Both sides pursued receiver quality rather than a positional swap. Scott gained sustained recorded utilization, while Stew's onward McConkey return requires attribution review. Draft round alone does not establish keeper cost.

analysis.headline: Stover Addresses Quarterback Need While Thommy Adds Backfield Depth
analysis.analysis: Week 1 Stover started Stafford for 4.10 points; McCaffrey and Kyren Williams occupied RB slots with Judkins in FLEX. Thommy started Dart for 25.60 while Lawrence scored 26.10 on the bench; Achane and Stevenson started at RB with Mason and Croskey-Merritt among reserves. Week 2 Lawrence started for Stover (6.16) while Stafford scored 26.98 on the bench. Judkins was on Thommy's bench (7.30), with Achane and Stevenson starting. The later archive shows Judkins 82.40 across seven starts and Lawrence 129.26 across eight. Compare QB and RB against appropriate alternatives, not raw points alone.
analysis.verdict: Stover converted a FLEX back into another quarterback option; Thommy moved quarterback depth into his backfield. Both strategies have a defensible roster rationale, but initial deployment and later scoring do not establish net lineup gains.

limitations: draft is initial baseline, not exact pretrade roster; preseason moves require replay
